scope: v2: recommendation consistency + tone + sample-vs-total + hedged-vs-asserted

findings.message: The 'Recommended Actions' section switches from third-person ('address the 96 WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility issues identified') to first-person implicit framing, but more critically the 'Summary of Findings' closing paragraph switches into first-person ('We invite the team') while the surrounding Findings body sections use third-person ('We identified', 'We recorded', 'We measured') — the Findings body is written in consultant first-person throughout, yet the 'What's Working Well' section and body priorities consistently use 'we', making the voice internally consistent there; however, the 'About This Report' section is written entirely in passive/third-person ('This report covers', 'Each page is analysed', 'Automated findings are reviewed') while the Findings priorities are written in first-person ('We identified', 'We recorded', 'We measured'), creating a material voice mismatch between the narrative introduction section and the Findings body sections of the same report.
findings.context: "This report covers 5 pages audited" (About This Report) vs "We identified 11 instances" (Priority 1) and "We recorded a Served HTML Discovery Readiness score" (Priority 5)

findings.message: Priority 6 (Metadata Stack Completeness — 51/100) is not explicitly addressed in any engagement phase in 'What's Next'; the Critical Fixes phase lists P1–P5 and Full Optimisation lists P1–P9, but Priority 6 is a distinct named finding that must appear in at least one phase by number, and it is absent from the Critical Fixes scope description which ends at P5.
findings.context: "Critical Fixes | P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 (Compliance Risk + Discovery)" — Priority 6 first appears only under Full Optimisation's catch-all P1–P9 label

findings.message: The 'Optional Enhancements' section states 'NEOM has no ratings anywhere' in effect by saying 'once Product entities are in place across the audited set, attaching AggregateRating markup…' — but the Structured Data Inventory table shows AggregateRating IS present on 3 of 3 product pages at 100% recommended coverage, meaning the enhancement recommendation contradicts the audit's own structured data findings and implies an absence that does not exist in the audited sample.
findings.context: "AggregateRating | 3 | 100% | 100%" (Structured Data Inventory) vs "attaching AggregateRating markup allows machines to surface star ratings" (Optional Enhancements)

findings.message: The sitemap section simultaneously grades the sitemap as both 'Complete' and 'Partial' in adjacent sentences, which is a material self-contradiction in a client-facing document that would confuse any reader relying on the grade to understand their sitemap status.
findings.context: "Sitemap grade:** Complete" followed immediately by "The sitemap carries a Partial grade, listing 908 URLs"
